title: The Hidden Risk of Vibe-Coded Apps
hook: Anyone can now describe an app and have AI build it — but the AI can quietly leave the doors unlocked. One builder ran his live site for months before noticing a gaping security hole.
key_points: 'Vibe coding' lets non-programmers build working apps by describing them to AI — code they can't fully read.
The Verge reports a builder ran his live site for months before finding a hidden SQL-injection flaw.
SQL injection lets attackers read, change, or wreck a site's database through ordinary input fields.
AI writes plausible-looking code, but plausible isn't secure — and a non-coder can't spot the gap.
Lesson: anything you vibe-code that handles real data or users deserves a security check.
content_html: AI has made it possible to build a working app without knowing how to code — you describe what you want, and a chatbot writes it. The Verge tells the story of a builder who vibe-coded a website and put it online right away, only to discover months later that it carried a hidden "SQL injection" vulnerability — a flaw that can let an attacker reach straight into a site's database.
extra_html: The catch with vibe coding is that the AI's code looks finished and runs fine, so there's nothing to tip off a non-programmer that something's wrong underneath. SQL injection is a classic example: if a site doesn't carefully handle what users type into its forms, an attacker can sneak in database commands and read, change, or delete data. A professional developer would normally check for this; someone who just asked an AI to "build me a site" usually doesn't know to look. None of this means vibe coding is useless — it's genuinely powerful for prototypes and personal projects. But the moment your app touches real user data, payments, or anything you'd be upset to lose, it's worth having someone (or a security tool) review what the AI actually wrote. The convenience is real; so is the responsibility that comes with shipping software.

related.title: Making Things Without Code
related.hook: Describe an app, a website, or a little tool in plain English, and AI will write the code and build a first version. 'Vibe coding' lets non-programmers make software — within limits.

related.title: Hype or Real?
related.hook: AI coverage swings between 'this changes everything' and 'it's all a bubble.' The truth is usually in between — and a few questions help you judge any big AI claim for yourself.

flashcards.prompt: Why can a 'vibe-coded' app be risky even when it runs perfectly?

choices.text: AI-written code can hide security flaws a non-coder can't see, like SQL injection
Apps built by AI never connect to the internet
AI code always refuses to handle user data

flashcards.explanation_html: The code looks finished and runs fine, so nothing tips off a non-programmer that something's wrong underneath — exactly how the hidden SQL-injection flaw slipped through.

flashcards.prompt: What is SQL injection, in plain terms?
flashcards.back_html: A flaw where an attacker slips database commands into ordinary input fields, letting them read, change, or delete a site's data.

flashcards.prompt: When should vibe-coded software get a security review?
flashcards.back_html: Whenever it touches real user data, payments, or anything you'd hate to lose — have a person or a security tool check what the AI actually wrote.
